The premise does not hold in this document. NFA-F did not show the best capacity retention. The authors report NFA-A as the most stable, and NFA-F as the weakest of the variants in the cycling test at C/3. The reported retention after the cycle count was ≈80% capacity after[1] for NFA-A, ≈70%[2] for the NFA 811[3] variant, and about ≈50%[4] for NFA-F.

The paper does not measure why NFA-F faded most. Its only explanation is a hypothesis: the increase in iron content may drive structural transitions that cause capacity fade during continuous cycling, and the authors say this iron redox process is still being investigated.[5] This fits NFA-F, which has the highest iron content of the variants: LiNi0.8Fe0.15Al0.05O2 (NFA-F)[6]
